body_markdown:
Zhao Yi


harshitha.rv@f…


Tue, 11/03/2026 - 11:13


**Where are you located? What geographical region(s) do you cover?**
I am based in Taiyuan, Shanxi, China. Over the past five years at Fortrea, I have supported monitoring activities across clinical research sites throughout China, working with a wide range of investigators, site teams, and study stakeholders. These experiences have given me a broad perspective on clinical research operations and allowed me to build strong relationships while contributing to the successful delivery of studies across different regions.


**How long have you been working in the area of clinical research?**
I have been working in clinical research for eight years, gaining experience in monitoring, site management and study execution across a variety of therapeutic areas and research settings.


**What is the best part of your job?**
One of the things I enjoy most about being a Clinical Research Associate is seeing how a clinical trial comes together through the efforts of many different people. The role requires a combination of scientific knowledge, attention to detail, communication skills and project awareness. Understanding complex protocols, identifying key details within source documentation, and working closely with investigators, site staff, sponsors and study teams all play an important part in helping studies progress. What makes the role especially rewarding is knowing that every monitoring visit, discussion and issue resolved contributes to the development of potential new therapies for patients.


**What has been interesting about your work in clinical research? Did anything surprise you about the patient population?**
What I find most interesting about clinical research is the people behind every study. Each participant has a unique story, and I am always impressed by the dedication shown by both patients and their families. Many participants join clinical trials not only in the hope of accessing new treatment options, but also because they want to contribute to medical progress and help future patients. Their commitment is inspiring and serves as a constant reminder that behind every protocol, data point and study milestone are real people placing their trust in clinical research.


**What are you most proud of in your work?**
I am most proud of the moments when a study reaches an important milestone. Clinical trials require significant planning, coordination and collaboration over many years. Whether it is site activation, enrollment completion, database lock, or overall study completion, each achievement represents meaningful progress toward bringing innovative treatments to patients. Being part of that journey is what continues to motivate me and reinforces the importance of the work we do every day.
I'm grateful for the opportunities I have had throughout my career and remain motivated by the chance to contribute to research that may ultimately improve patients' lives and advance the future of medicine.
